newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: PRESS DIGEST - Philippine newspapers - June 6.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Philippine newspapers - June 6.

text.p: These are the leading stories in Manila newspapers on Friday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- The first Filipino extradited from the United States has pleaded not guilty to charges of involvement in a multi-million peso Treasury bills scam. Marilyn Nite, president of the defunct Bancapital Development Corp, was escorted back to Manila on Thursday from San Francisco by agents of the National Bureau of Investigation. (ALL NEWSPAPERS)

- Moves for a united opposition and a common presidential candidate for next year's election suffered a setback as Senator Miriam Defensor Santiago withdrew from the talks saying that she was led to believe that all parties would be given equal chances of fielding the common presidential candidate. (ALL NEWSPAPERS)

- The Office of the Ombudsman filed graft charges against 30 people, 20 of them Quezon City officials, and six owners of the Ozone Disco for the fire which gutted the night spot and killed 162 people in March last year. (PHILIPPINE STAR)
- A mystery man who met slained journalist Danny Hernandez in a Pasay City bar the night before he was shot could have masterminded his killing. (INQUIRER)
- The NBI has invited eight more people for questioning on the death of Hernandez. (MANILA CHRONICLE)

- The Philippine's national inflation rate hit a 10-year low of 4.2 percent in May, down from 4.6 percent. Exports grew by nearly 23 percent to $7.588 billion in the first four months of the year compared to $6.177 billion a year earlier, the National Statistics Office said. (ALL NEWSPAPERS)

- Trade Secretary Cesar Bautista is recommending to President Fidel Ramos the immediate review of tariff rates, incentives, trade agreements and a halt in the proliferation of duty-free shops to correct the downtrend in industrial growth. (MALAYA)
- Victorias Milling Co is working out a new 90-day debt moratorium. (MANILA TIMES)
